title: Tierpark Bern Dählhölzli, Neu- und Ersatzbauten, 291 Architekturleistungen, Studienauftrag mit 2 Lose
description:
La Ville de Berne gère plusieurs installations zoologiques sous le nom de « Tierpark Bern » (Parc zoologique de Berne). Elle offre à la population des possibilités de détente et des expériences personnelles, transmet et développe des connaissances sur la faune et la flore, et sensibilise le public à la détention des animaux dans le respect de leurs besoins, ainsi qu’à la protection de la nature et des espèces. Le Tierpark Bern comprend notamment les sites du Dählhölzli et du Parc aux ours (Bären Park). Afin de répondre aux besoins d’un nombre croissant de visiteurs et d’assurer une détention des animaux adaptée à leurs besoins, des investissements sont prévus dans les infrastructures et les enclos existants ainsi que dans de nouvelles installations. Par ailleurs, des mesures sont envisagées pour améliorer les conditions de travail du personnel. Parallèlement, le Tierpark Bern entend accorder une attention accrue, à l’avenir, aux défis posés par le changement climatique et la perte de biodiversité. Le périmètre du projet abrite en outre des habitats et des espèces protégés par la Loi fédérale sur la protection de la nature et du paysage (LPN) ; leur préservation, ou une compensation équivalente, doit impérativement être prise en compte lors du développement du projet.


La réalisation de ces objectifs implique des transformations spatiales. Il s’agit de créer de nouvelles installations et de remplacer celles qui sont vétustes. De plus, l’accès au site du Dählhölzli doit être amélioré pour les personnes en situation de handicap. Cette démarche constitue un élément essentiel de la planification globale du Tierpark Bern pour la période 2023–2033, laquelle décrit en détail la vision et la stratégie de ce qui se veut être « le parc zoologique le plus charmant de Suisse ».

description: Special Notice: Virtual Industry Day Event Schedule & Platform Date of Event: December 10, 2026 (Thursday) Time: 1:00 PM � 2:00 PM Pacific Standard Time (PST) Location/Platform: Virtual via Microsoft Teams (see below for details) Purpose of Event The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, Sacramento District (USACE-SPK) is pleased to announce a virtual Industry Day on December 10, 2026. The purpose of this session is to provide industry partners with a comprehensive overview of the upcoming Geotechnical Drilling Multiple Award Task Order Contract (MATOC). The Government will present details regarding program requirements, anticipated geographic scope, proposed technical evaluation factors (such as specialized rig fleet inventory and AASHTO/USACE MTC laboratory accreditation standards), and the tentative acquisition milestone schedule. USACE-SPK anticipates issuing a formal solicitation under NAICS 541360in February 2027., and highly encourage participation from regional small businesses, prospective joint venture partners, and specialty subcontractors who intend to compete. Scope of Work and Technical Capabilities USACE-SPK seeks firms with the capabilities to provide comprehensive geotechnical drilling, cone penetrometer testing (CPT) services, and test-pit excavations utilizing backhoes and track hoes. The principal features of the work encompass soil drilling and sampling utilizing hollow-stem flight augers, solid-stem flight augers, mud-rotary, air-rotary, and percussion drilling methods, including ODEX, Down-hole Casing Advance Systems, or other specialized percussion drilling systems. Contract requirements will also mandate sonic drilling and sampling, alongside rock core drilling and sampling of up to 6-inch diameter using wireline or conventional diamond-impregnated drill bits. Soil sampling operations will require standard penetrometers and other split-barrel samplers up to 3-inch-diameter, as well as undisturbed soil sampling using Shelby push tubes and Pitcher barrels with Pitcher tubes. Field operations will further include CPT testing, piezometer and inclinometer installations, hydraulic pressure testing associated with rock core drilling, and observation well installation and development, which includes pump, permeability, and percolation testing. Contractors will be responsible for generating all associated documentation, to include detailed drill logs, trench or test-pit logs, as-built diagrams for all instrumentation and well installations, and percolation test records. Additionally, the contractor must occasionally furnish the professional services of a registered, licensed Geologist or Geotechnical Engineer. Furthermore, firms must possess the capability to provide certified geotechnical laboratory services. The required testing scope includes moisture content, soil classification, sieve analysis, hydrometer, Atterberg limits, consolidation, triaxial testing, direct shear, California Bearing Ratio (CBR), organic content, and Specific Gravity. To ensure data integrity, all laboratory testing must be performed by a facility accredited by the American Association of State Highway and Transportation Officials (AASHTO) in accordance with the corresponding ASTM standards. Finally, the laboratory must be, or successfully become, validated by the USACE Materials Testing Center (MTC) for all requested testing methods. title: 652-25-111 Repair USP 800 AC-59
TECHNOLOGY LICENSING OPPORTUNITY: SonicCoat
description: Non-Invasive Ultrasonic Coating Evaluation for Electrochemical Systems Makers of fuel cells, electrolyzers and other electrochemical devices depend on catalyst coatings applied with tight consistency; yet, today�s inspection tools force production to pause so samples can be pulled and studied in a laboratory. SonicCoat, developed by researchers at Los Alamos National Laboratory, offers a faster path: A gentle ultrasonic probe reads how much catalyst has been laid down while the coating line keeps running, giving producers real-time confidence in every layer without slowing throughput or harming the part. The payoff is higher yield, more uniform device performance and lower material cost across a platform that reaches from clean-energy hardware to batteries, solar films and semiconductors. How it Works The SonicCoat method rests on a simple physical fact: Sound travels through an object differently as the object�s makeup changes. A small transducer sends acoustic waves through a coated part and listens for the natural tones, or resonances, that the material rings back. As the catalyst is sprayed onto the surface layer by layer, those resonant tones shift in pitch and loudness in step with how much material has been added, so the acoustic signature becomes a fingerprint of coating thickness and uniformity. Because the reading is taken by sound rather than by scraping, cutting or exposing the part to X-rays, the inspection happens in place and in seconds, and the part continues down the line unharmed. Technology Description SonicCoat applies Acoustic Resonance Spectroscopy (ARS) to the quality control of catalyst-coated gas diffusion layers, the porous electrodes at the heart of fuel cells and electrolyzers. A coated sample is held in fixturing fitted with transducers that excite it across a broad frequency band and record its resonant response, first as a baseline on the bare substrate and then after each successive catalyst layer. Comparing each response against the baseline reveals how the resonance peaks migrate and change in amplitude, and those movements track the amount of platinum catalyst deposited. Testing has shown peaks moving roughly in proportion to added catalyst content, which demonstrates enough sensitivity to distinguish layer-by-layer differences in loading. Because the measurement is non-destructive and adds little time to the coating cycle, the approach fits directly into continuous production rather than diverting samples for laboratory analysis by scanning electron microscopy, energy dispersive X-ray spectroscopy or X-ray fluorescence, the after-the-fact methods relied on today. Catalyst loading is a primary driver of both cost and performance in electrochemical devices, so verified, consistent deposition translates into steadier power output, longer service life and less wasted precious metal. The same principle extends to any process where a thin coating must be monitored on a substrate, and the technique suits scale-up because it neither caps throughput nor limits the number of parts that can be checked. Advantages Inspects coatings in place while the line keeps moving, with no need to stop and pull samples Fully non-destructive, so parts are never cut, scraped or exposed to X-rays Reads catalyst buildup layer by layer for tight, repeatable quality control Relies on simple, low-cost ultrasonic hardware instead of large laboratory instruments Protects costly materials such as platinum by catching over-coating or under-coating early Scales to high-volume production without limiting output Market Applications Fuel Cell and Electrolyzer Manufacturing Battery Manufacturing Solar Energy Semiconductor Fabrication Protective Coatings TRL 4 U.S. Patent pending LA-UR-26-28073 LANL Tech Partnerships: Unlock the Innovative Potential Los Alamos National Laboratory offers a wide range of cutting-edge technologies and capabilities that may provide your company with a competitive edge in the market and unlock the innovative potential that can enhance, refine, and revolutionize your products. Dans le cadre de l'évolution de leur flotte, de l'augmentation des exigences de qualité de lavage et du renouvellement d'équipements arrivés en fin de vie technique, les TL ont décidé de procéder au renouvellement de leurs installations de lavage. Cette démarche vise à garantir la disponibilité à long terme des équipements, à améliorer la qualité du nettoyage des véhicules et à répondre aux besoins futurs de l'exploitation.

Le présent appel d'offres porte sur le démontage, la fourniture, la livraison, le montage, les essais, la mise en service, la formation ainsi que les prestations de garantie associées aux nouvelles installations de lavage des dépôts de Perrelet et de la Borde.

L'acquisition qui sera mise en concurrence concerne des installations de lavage industrielles destinées au nettoyage de véhicules routiers de transport public, comprenant notamment :

  • des installations de lavage 2 côtés ;
  • des installations de lavage 4 côtés ;
  • des systèmes de lavage sous-châssis ;
  • des équipements de prélavage et de rinçage ;
  • des systèmes de production d'eau osmosée ;
  • des automatismes et systèmes de supervision ;
  • des interfaces avec les systèmes d'information des T L.

Les futures installations devront être compatibles avec l'ensemble du parc de véhicules des T L, y compris les autobus standards, les autobus articulés, les trolleybus articulés, les trolleybus bi-articulés ainsi que les futurs véhicules électriques.

Le marché est attribué sous la forme d'un contrat clé en main. Le fournisseur retenu sera responsable de la conception détaillée, de la fabrication, de la fourniture, du montage, des essais, de la mise en service ainsi que de la formation du personnel d'exploitation et de maintenance.

title: Refurbishment and Modernisation (RM4S) - Scotland Framework Agreement
description: LHC Procurement Group Limited (LHCPG) is procuring the Refurbishment and Modernisation Scotland Framework Agreement (RM4S) on behalf of the Scottish Procurement Alliance (SPA). LHCPG is acting as the Contracting Authority and central purchasing body for this procurement. The Framework is being procured solely for use in Scotland and will provide eligible public sector organisations with a compliant and flexible route for the delivery of refurbishment, improvement, repair, maintenance and modernisation works, goods and associated services across residential and non-residential buildings. The procurement is being conducted using the Open Procedure in accordance with the Procurement Act 2023 and the Procurement Regulations 2024. When awarding Call-Off Contracts, eligible Clients and Partners must also comply with the Framework Agreement, the applicable Call-Off procedure and any other procurement legislation applicable to them. RM4S builds upon the existing Refurbishment and Modernisation Framework and has been developed following market engagement with suppliers and public sector organisations. Feedback received through that engagement has informed the scope, Workstreams, Lot structure, value bands and regional arrangements. The Framework comprises the following Workstreams and Lots: Painting and Decorating Electrical Works, from zero to 500k Electrical Works, 500k and above Kitchens and Bathrooms, from zero to 500k Kitchens and Bathrooms, 500k to 2m Kitchens and Bathrooms, 2m and above Aids and Adaptations Damp and Mould Remediation Environmental and External Works, External Works Environmental and External Works, Grounds Maintenance Stoneworks Reactive Repairs and Maintenance Multi-Disciplinary Works, from zero to 750k Multi-Disciplinary Works, 750k to 2.5m Multi-Disciplinary Works, 2.5m and above Kitchens (Supply only) The scope may include planned and reactive maintenance, refurbishment and improvement programmes, component replacement, compliance-led works, accessibility adaptations, environmental and external works, property modernisation and wider asset management and investment programmes. Each Lot is divided into five regional areas covering North Eastern Scotland, Highlands and Islands, Eastern Scotland, West Central Scotland and Southern Scotland. Bidders may apply for one or more Lots and regional areas in accordance with the Procurement Documents. Subject to there being sufficient Qualifying Bidders, LHCPG will appoint no more than 10 Appointed Companies for each Lot and regional area. Where a Micro and Small Enterprise Reserved Allocation applies, it forms part of, and is not additional to, the maximum of 10 appointments. The Framework will not operate a reserve list and no additional or replacement Bidders may be appointed during the Framework Term. The Framework is structured to support participation from organisations of different sizes and capabilities through its Workstreams, value bands, regional areas and applicable Micro and Small Enterprise Reserved Allocations. All Bidders will remain subject to the same published qualification, compliance, quality, evaluation and appointment requirements. RM4S is intended to support the delivery of high-quality and compliant solutions, sustainable supply chains, environmental improvement, social value, community benefits, Fair Work and proportionate innovation. Detailed technical requirements, eligibility provisions, award criteria, appointment methodology and Call-Off procedures are set out in the Procurement Documents.

title: Restauration de la libre circulation des poissons / Réfection des centrales électriques / Renouvellement de la concession, phases SIA 32 à 53
description:
L'objectif principal du projet est de garantir, à partir de 2030 environ, une production d'énergie renouvelable issue de l'hydroélectricité qui soit durable à long terme et économiquement viable. Cela comprend les objectifs partiels suivants :

  1. La concession pour l'exploitation de l'énergie hydraulique des centrales d'Obertöss et de Niedertöss est garantie pour au moins 40 ans supplémentaires, dans des conditions-cadres économiquement viables. En outre, il doit être possible de constituer une provision pour le démantèlement des installations à l’expiration de la concession.
  2. Les exigences légales en matière de restauration de la libre circulation des poissons seront respectées, en garantissant la prise en charge intégrale des coûts par la Confédération.
  3. La protection des monuments historiques sera réglementée de manière contraignante et à long terme dans le cadre des objectifs partiels 1) et 2). Un développement et une modernisation modérés des installations des centrales électriques pendant la durée de la concession doivent être garantis.

title: TECHNOLOGY LICENSING OPPORTUNITY: Multi-Channel Atomic Magnetometer (MCAM)
description: Unlike conventional multichannel atomic magnetometers that require one vapor cell and one optical system for each sensing channel, the patented Multi-Channel Atomic Magnetometer (MCAM) architecture from Los Alamos National Laboratory replaces many independent atomic magnetometers with a single shared vapor cell and optical system that simultaneously generates multiple independent sensing channels. MCAM is a non-cryogenic multi-channel optical quantum sensor in a single module that captures ultra-faint biomagnetic signals from the brain, heart and other sources with sensitivity approaching that of the cryogenic SQUID-based systems that have defined the field for decades. MCAM delivers that performance at roughly one-tenth the per-channel cost without a drop of liquid helium. The module pairs one large alkali-metal vapor cell with broad pump and probe laser beams read out by a photodiode array, providing 16 independent sensing channels in a single housing, scaling into helmet-style arrays of hundreds of channels, and flexing around the patient rather than forcing the patient into a fixed cryogenic dewar. Together, these attributes more easily allow for magnetoencephalography, magnetocardiography and magnetic-particle imaging while accelerating overall magnetic imaging workflows. Ongoing development is aimed at extending the sensing architecture from the centimeter scale characterized in the current prototype toward micrometer-scale spatial resolution, opening a path into cellular-scale magnetic imaging that current cryogenic and room-temperature arrays cannot address. How it Works The MCAM module operates on the spin-exchange relaxation-free (SERF) regime, in which atomic spins of alkali-metal atoms inside a large, sealed vapor cell are aligned by a circularly polarized broad pump laser beam through optical pumping and then interrogated by a linearly polarized broad probe beam propagating along a nearly parallel path. An external magnetic field of interest tilts the aligned atomic spins by an angle proportional to the field strength, and that tilt rotates the polarization plane of the probe beam through the Faraday effect; a photodiode array reads the optical rotation simultaneously at multiple points across the cell, with each photodiode pixel reporting on its own localized sensing volume. A buffer gas inside the cell restricts atomic motion so that the small cell volumes behind each pixel behave as independent sensing channels, a rear mirror folds the beams back through the cell to shorten the stand-off distance to the magnetic source, and transparent Pyrex wire heaters hold the cell at the operating temperature needed for SERF operation. Technology Description The patented shared-cell architecture generates multiple independent sensing channels from a single vapor cell, a single pump beam, a single probe beam, and a single detector array. A pair of broad, co-propagating laser beams, one for optical pumping and the other for probing, traverses the shared vapor cell to manipulate the internal atomic spins, converting the local magnetic field distribution into a spatially resolved optical signal that is read out by a multi-pixel photodetector. Because the buffer gas inside the cell restricts atomic diffusion, each pixel of the detector reports on its own small, spatially distinct region of the cell; therefore, the single module yields a two-dimensional map of the local magnetic field rather than a single-point measurement. Operation in the SERF regime, together with an integrated heating and shielding arrangement and a fold-back optical geometry that shortens the distance from the sensing volume to the magnetic source, sets the sensitivity floor in the low tens of femtotesla per root hertz at low frequency. A development path has been identified to reduce the effective sensing-volume scale from the roughly 1 cm per-channel footprint of the current prototype toward the 1 ?m range, which would extend the platform from whole-organ mapping into micro-scale magnetic imaging regimes. Architecturally, the MCAM module is engineered for arrays. Because all channels within a single module share one vapor cell, one laser pair, and one optics assembly, the per-channel parts count and tuning effort drop sharply versus designs that stack many single-channel sensors. Fiber-optic coupling between the laser sources and each sensor head lets modules be repositioned independently, so many modules can be tiled into a conformal helmet or surface array that adapts to head or torso shape and supports configurations that rigid large-cell predecessors cannot accommodate. The design is compatible with several alkali-metal and buffer-gas options and with per-module bias coils that allow each module to be tuned individually inside a larger array. Advantages Development path toward micrometer-scale spatial resolution, a roughly four-order-of-magnitude improvement over the current centimeter-scale prototype and an enabler of cellular-scale magnetic imaging Sensitivity at the low tens of femtotesla per root hertz, comparable to cryogenic SQUID arrays, while using a warm vapor, non-cryogenic architecture Roughly tenfold per-channel cost reduction by sharing one vapor cell, one laser pair and one optics set across 16 channels No liquid cryogens, eliminating recurring cryogen costs and simplifying siting, maintenance and shielding Fiber-coupled, repositionable sensor heads that conform to the patient rather than forcing the patient into a fixed dewar Scalable into helmet-style arrays of hundreds of channels, including a size-adjustable pediatric configuration Shorter sensor-to-source stand-off via rear-mirror beam folding, sharpening spatial resolution of biomagnetic sources Market Applications Medical Diagnostic Imaging (magnetoencephalography systems for epilepsy, stroke and neurodegenerative workups; magnetocardiography for arrhythmia and ischemia screening) Pediatric and Adaptive Neuroimaging (size-adjustable MEG helmets, point-of-care brain monitoring) Micro-scale Biomagnetic Imaging (single-neuron and small-circuit brain activity mapping, high-resolution cardiac tissue mapping) Cancer Diagnostics (magnetic nanoparticle imaging for tumor localization and targeted-therapy tracking) Magnetic Resonance Imaging (low-field/ultra-low field, portable MRI, functional brain imaging) Sensing (low-frequency antennas for underground or undersea links, geomagnetic surveying) Instrumentation (fundamental physics, biomagnetism laboratories, multichannel sensor R&D) Development Status: TRL 4 U.S. Patent No. 11,105,865 LA-UR-26-25904 LANL Tech Partnerships: Unlock the Innovative Potential Los Alamos National Laboratory offers a wide range of cutting-edge technologies and capabilities that may provide your company with a competitive edge in the market and unlock the innovative potential that can enhance, refine, and revolutionize your products. Dans le cadre du projet « ROKS-TP7 Centrale de dotation d'Ova Spin », l'installation de dotation, composée d'un groupe de machines comprenant une turbine, un générateur, une vanne sphérique, la conduite forcée et l'unité de contrôle commande datant de la mise en service initiale en 1968, va faire l'objet d'une révision complète après plus de 50 ans de fonctionnement.


L'objectif de cette révision complète de la turbine de dotation est de la mettre à niveau avec l'état actuel de la technique et de la remettre en parfait état mécanique.

La turbine de dotation a fait l’objet d’une révision partielle pour la dernière fois en 2002.


En résumé, les travaux principaux suivants sont prévus :

- Révision complète du générateur existant. Ce point ne fait pas partie de cet appel d’offres, mais fait l’objet d’un lot distinct

- Révision complète de la turbine avec renouvellement intégral de la protection anticorrosion

- Utilisation de la roue de rechange existante, des aubes directrices de rechange ainsi que d’autres pièces de rechange disponibles

- Enlèvement et élimination des peintures contenant des PCB

- Éventuellement, un nouvel échangeur de chaleur pour l'huile du palier de la turbine

- Remplacement de l’ancienne instrumentation


Caractéristiques techniques de la turbine de dotation :

Turbine Francis horizontale

Marque/type : Bell

Débit d'eau : 0,9 m³/s

Hauteur de chute : 57,64 m

Puissance : 500 kW

Mise en service : décembre 1968

Dernière révision : 2002

Vitesse de rotation : 750 tr/min

En raison des travaux de révision, de modernisation et de transformation de nos propres véhicules ferroviaires, ainsi que des pics de demande liés à une activité accrue dans le domaine de la construction des voies ferrées, les besoins en véhicules ne peuvent toutefois pas toujours être entièrement couverts par nos propres moyens de traction, ce qui rend inévitable la location de véhicules ferroviaires externes.

Afin de pouvoir répondre à tout moment aux besoins futurs, les catégories ou lots suivants doivent faire l’objet d’un appel d’offres:

  • Lot 1: Véhicules de traction purement thermiques, classe de puissance > 900 kW
  • Lot 2: Véhicules de traction purement thermiques, classe de puissance < 900 kW
  • Lot 3: Véhicules de traction purement thermiques, classe de puissance < 900 kW, équipés d’une grue
  • Lot 4: Véhicules de traction électriques/thermiques, classe de puissance électrique > 1000 kW et thermique > 200 kW
  • Lot 5: Véhicules de traction électriques/à batterie, classe de puissance électrique > 1000 kW et à batterie > 300 kW
  • Lot 6: Véhicules de traction électriques, classe de puissance électrique > 1000 kW

 

Les conditions suivantes doivent être respectées lors de la soumission des offres de lots:

  • Au total, les offres peuvent porter sur 6 lots, conformément au document 3.1 «Cahier des charges» et au document 2.1 «Fiche tarifaire».
  • Les prestations faisant l’objet de l’appel d’offres pour chaque lot proposé doivent impérativement être proposées.
  • Les offres sont autorisées aussi bien pour un seul lot que pour plusieurs lots.
  • Les soumissionnaires peuvent obtenir des adjudications pour plusieurs lots.
  • Les lots sont évalués et attribués indépendamment les uns des autres.
  • Les offres globales (forfaits portant sur plusieurs lots ou sur l’ensemble des lots) ne sont pas autorisées (voir également le point 4.1.6 du document 1.1 «Dispositions de procédure»). 

 

Adjudication et nombre d’adjudications

Conformément à l’article 32 de la loi fédérale sur les marchés publics (LMP), BLS se réserve le droit d’attribuer le marché à plusieurs soumissionnaires au sein de chaque lot afin de garantir la sécurité d’approvisionnement. Quatre (4) adjudications au maximum sont attribuées par lot conformément à l’art. 32, al. 2, LMP.

Les contrats-cadres sont conclus avec les adjudicataires après l’entrée en vigueur des adjudications.

Pour plus d’informations, veuillez notamment vous reporter au document 1.1 «Dispositions procédurales».
